findings.title: ACP cleanup can hang daemon shutdown on inherited pipe endpoints
findings.summary: Must-fix; rubric item 25; confidence 9/10. [STATIC INFERENCE, not executed] A caller-selected adapter or its tool can double-fork/setsid and orphan a process retaining adapter stdout/stderr or a stdin reader. ProcessTree only discovers current known ancestry or the original session, so that process can remain uncaptured. Explicit acp-close kills/reaps the known tree but then unconditionally joins blocking pipe workers. The two-second deadline only bounds checking known process termination, not these joins. A retained endpoint prevents EOF or write completion, so close never returns. Shutdown waits for that request connection to retire and also synchronously joins ACP cleanup, allowing one target to prevent daemon exit and socket/resource retirement. This affected unchanged-runtime defect is not introduced by the S04 test-only changes. It is an operational availability failure, not a claim that same-user tools are sandboxed.

locations.role: Known-tree cleanup followed by unconditional pipe-worker joins
Blocking stdout/stderr reads have no cancellation wakeup
Blocking stdin write can likewise retain a worker
Discovery excludes already-orphaned processes outside the original session
Close request waits synchronously for broker cleanup
Shutdown waits for request retirement and ACP cleanup
Current descendant fixtures use null stdio and do not exercise retained endpoints

evidence.label: Concrete source-to-sink path
evidence.explanation: An adapter-owned daemonized descendant can retain stdout/stderr without emitting data. After its intermediary exits and it leaves the original session, neither discovery predicate includes it. The captured tree can be fully terminated while the reader remains blocked in fill_buf/read or the stderr drainer in read. There is no independent cancellation of those descriptors before joining workers.

evidence.label: Nearby bounds do not bound the joins
evidence.explanation: The two-second deadline applies only to tree.terminated(). Condvar notification cannot wake blocking pipe I/O. The cleanup failure category is assigned only after all joins return, so this path never reaches an explicit incomplete-cleanup result.

evidence.label: Consumer consequence and coverage gap
evidence.explanation: acp_action synchronously calls cleanup for close. Daemon shutdown closes sockets but then waits for the request slots to disappear; socket shutdown cannot interrupt an ACP pipe join inside that request. Direct daemon shutdown also calls Broker::shutdown and cleanup. Current S04 descendants have null stdio, so their passing cleanup assertions do not cover this failure. README's honest orphan-capture limitation does not provide an escape from the unbounded join.

findings.remediation: Make ACP stdio workers interruptible independently of peer EOF, for example with nonblocking readiness polling and an explicit cancellation wakeup, so explicit close can always retire and join its workers even when another process retains an endpoint. Preserve truthful incomplete process cleanup and capacity charging instead of detaching workers or fabricating descendant death. Add a real-child regression that deliberately retains a pipe endpoint outside captured ancestry/session, observes bounded close/shutdown and worker retirement, then independently reaps that fixture.
